passages.excerpt_preview: It traces land acquisition and dispossession of mainly adivasi cultivators by TISCO from about 1900 to 1930.
British firms competed quickly for valuable mineral resources, and the Tatas needed collaboration with princely rulers and local intermediaries.
round 1900 Jamsetji Tata sent Dorabji Tata and Shapurji Saklatvala to seek prospecting licenses for iron ore, coal, copper and manganese.
The article characterizes Jamshedpur as the site of an Indian firm’s first company town and of major mineral extraction.
